newsitem.title: THAILAND: Lehman sees spread on Thai Yankee bond tightening.
newsitem.headline: Lehman sees spread on Thai Yankee bond tightening.

text.p: The Kingdom of Thailand's US$600 million Yankee bond launched earlier this month will trade successfully in the secondary market with the spread likely to tighten by 10-15 basis points by the end of this year, joint-lead manager Lehman Brothers said on Monday.
Stephen Taran, senior vice president and credit research manager at Lehman, said investors were confident the government was addressing Thailand's short-term economic problems.
"The spread has tightened to 86-88 basis points and should continue to tighten over time," he said. The issue was launched at a spread of 90 basis points over Treasuries.

"This will happen on the back of growing evidence that the government short-term adjustment policies are working, the continuing consolidation in the financial sector and increased recognition that the government's strategy to address structural problems is credible," he added.
The issue was launched on April 10 and has a 7.75 percent coupon.
Although the spread was higher than the 75-80 points anticipated by the market earlier, analysts hailed the debut as successful as the bond was twice oversubscribed.

The launch was clouded by various negative factors such as the credit downgrade by Moody's Investors Service, S&P's credit downgrade of two major Thai commercial banks and the hike in U.S. interest rates.
The battered financial sector which is facing rising non-performing loans due to over-exposure to the ailing property sector was also a minus point.

Among the concerns raised by investors are Thailand's large current account deficit which stood above eight percent of the GDP in 1996, poor export performance, and looming financial sector melt-down.
Taran said the Thai government had done a good job in dispelling investors' misconceptions about Thailand by assuring them the government's policy was credible, comprehensive and coherent.
Moreover, investors were convinced the country's economic fundamentals remained strong.

He said the Yankee bonds would provide a good benchmark for corporates wanting to issue the same kind of debt. The unmet demand for the deal would also spill over into increased demand for bonds sold by other Thai issuers, he added.
